(Define the weight of a graph to be the sum of the weights of the vertices and edges of that graph.)  prove this is NP-Complete

message.content:
The problem is in NP.
We can verify a solution quickly.
A certificate lists specific vertices and edges.
Summing their weights takes polynomial time.
Thus membership in NP holds true.
Now we prove NP-hardness via reduction.
We reduce from Subset Sum Problem.
Given numbers $a_1, \dots, a_n$ and target $B$.
Construct graph with one vertex per number.
Vertex $v_i$ has weight $a_i$.
Add isolated vertices to ensure structure.
No edges exist between any two vertices.
Total weight of subgraph is sum of chosen vertices.
This exactly matches the Subset Sum instance.
If subset sums to $B$, subgraph exists.
Conversely, valid subgraph implies valid subset exists.
Therefore, Subset Sum reduces to this problem.
Since Subset Sum is NP-complete, this follows.
The reduction runs in polynomial time easily.
Hence the weighted subgraph problem is NP-hard.
Combined with NP membership, it is NP-complete.
